newsitem.title: USA: GRC Int'l sees Q4 shr $0.09 to $0.11.
newsitem.headline: GRC Int'l sees Q4 shr $0.09 to $0.11.

text.p: A top executive of GRC International Inc on Monday predicted that the company would post fourth quarter earnings from continuing operations of $0.09 to $0.11 per share, marking GRC's second consecutive profitable quarter.

"I'm very bullish looking forward into the next year," GRC president and chief executive Jim Roth told Reuters in an interview. The information technology company expects to report earnings on August 14.

In addition, Roth forecast fourth quarter revenue in a range of $30 million to $31 million, a figure he said included neither gains nor charges from discontinued operations, and 1997 revenue of $117 million to $118 million.
"The last two quarters in my opinion represent a complete turn-around," Roth said.

GRC dipped into negative territory during its first fiscal quarter of 1997 when it posted losses of $0.28 per share, a slide it attributed to its investments in commercial telecommunications products.

Since then, the company has sold its Dynatup materials testing business unit and shut down its Telecommunications Division. The company returned to profitability last quarter, reporting earnings of $0.06 per share on revenues of $29 million.
Roth said he based his positive forecast on the company's forward momentum as evidenced by a large backlog.
"Our current maximum backlog with all of the options is numerically the largest I've seen and it's more than three years of revenue," he said.
When asked if the figure was in the range of $400 million Roth initially declined to comment, but later said, "It's on the order of the figure you mentioned."
